The chr rule

Source: vignettes/chr-rule.Rmd
chr-rule.Rmd

The constant harvest rate (chr) rule (ICES 2025, method 2.2) is for category 3 stocks with medium growth (0.32 ≤ K < 0.45). The advice is the last index value times a harvest rate:

Ay+1=Iy×Fproxy×b×mA_{y+1} = I_{y} \times F_{proxy} \times b \times m

  • FproxyF_{proxy}: the harvest rate proxy, the mean of catch / index over the reference years in which the mean length of the catch above Lc is above LF=M (f = Lmean / LF=M > 1);
  • bb: the biomass safeguard, as in the rfb rule;
  • mm: the multiplier, 0.5 for 0.32 ≤ K < 0.45;

followed by the stability clause (+20% / −30%, not applied when b<1b < 1).

At MFRI the chr rule is used for whiting (04-whg). This vignette follows 04-whg’s pipeline on simulated data; the numbers belong to no stock.

library(dlsrules)

Simulated data

A biomass index (in the stock repos: the spring survey biomass of whiting over 40 cm, smb_b40, from pax::pax_si_length_index()), the landings, and the catch length distribution by year.

set.seed(4)
years <- 1985:2026
e <- stats::filter(rnorm(length(years), 0, 0.25), 0.7, method = "recursive")
index <- data.frame(year = years, index = round(8000 * exp(as.numeric(e))))

landings <- data.frame(
  year = 1985:2025,
  landings = round(index$index[1:41] * runif(41, 0.15, 0.45))
)

z <- 0.25 + 0.15 * sin(seq_along(1985:2025) / 5)
ldist <- expand.grid(length = 20:75, year = 1985:2025)
ldist$n <- round(
  3000 * plogis((ldist$length - 38) / 1.5) *
    exp(-z[ldist$year - 1984] * (ldist$length - 38) / 2 * (ldist$length > 38))
)
ldist <- ldist[, c("year", "length", "n")]

The index has a value for the assessment year (2026, the spring survey of the assessment year), the landings and lengths stop the year before. In a stock repo ldist is catch_ldist() of the pax_db target (see vignette("rfb-rule") for why it does not raise the counts again), and the landings are all countries’ landings in 5.a in tonnes.

Harvest rate proxy

Linf for whiting is a high quantile of the lengths in the catch, because the growth parameters of the stock are not reliable. 04-whg uses the 99.8% quantile (the largest length was unreasonably high); p = 1 gives the largest length.

assessment_year <- 2026
Lc <- 39
Linf <- linf_from_catch(ldist, p = 0.998)
Linf
#> [1] 75
hr <- harvest_rate_proxy(
  ldist,
  index,
  landings,
  Lc = Lc,
  Linf = Linf,
  hr_years = 1985:(assessment_year - 1)
)
head(hr)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 7
#>    year     L     f index landings    hr used 
#>   <int> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>    <dbl> <dbl> <lgl>
#> 1  1985  46.7 0.974  8445     3552 0.421 FALSE
#> 2  1986  46.2 0.962  7255     1216 0.168 FALSE
#> 3  1987  45.7 0.952  9336     1528 0.164 FALSE
#> 4  1988  45.3 0.945 10345     4621 0.447 FALSE
#> 5  1989  45.1 0.939 14415     3052 0.212 FALSE
#> 6  1990  44.9 0.935 14353     6153 0.429 FALSE
attr(hr, "hr_proxy")
#> [1] 0.2967323

The result has one row per year with length data; used marks the reference years (in hr_years and f > 1). The proxy is the mean of hr over those years, kept as the attribute hr_proxy, with Lc, Linf and LF=M in the attributes lc, linf and lfm for the tech report figures.

hr[hr$used, c("year", "f", "hr")]

#>    <int> <dbl> <dbl>

#>  6  2006  1.09 0.322

Reference points and advice

The chr rule needs K (for the multiplier) and Itrigger. Iloss is computed from the index up to the assessment year:

ref_points <- ref_points_iloss(
  list(K = 0.38),
  index[index$year <= assessment_year, ],
  method = "min",
  itrigger_factor = 1.4
)
str(ref_points)
#> List of 4
#>  $ K         : num 0.38
#>  $ I_lim     : num 6228
#>  $ I_lim_year: int 2018
#>  $ I_trigger : num 8719

chr_advice() cuts the index at the assessment year, runs fproxy_rule() and returns the components with lower-case names. It is the chr_prognosis target of 04-whg, and feeds hafroreports::hr_advice_table_chr() and advice_hist_rows().

prognosis <- chr_advice(
  index,
  prev_tac = 1320,
  hr_proxy = attr(hr, "hr_proxy"),
  ref_points = ref_points,
  assessment_year = assessment_year
)
#> [1] "'K' is greater than 0.32 therefore apply the CHR rule"
prognosis
#> # A tibble: 12 × 4
#>    component                   value type                     assessment_year
#>    <chr>                       <dbl> <chr>                              <dbl>
#>  1 previous_catch_advice    1320     advice                              2026
#>  2 biomass_index            9775     biomass_index                       2026
#>  3 Fmsy_proxy                  0.297 fishing_pressure_proxy              2026
#>  4 last_index_value         9775     biomass_safeguard                   2026
#>  5 Itrigger                 8719     biomass_safeguard                   2026
#>  6 Iloss                    6228     biomass_safeguard                   2026
#>  7 biomass_safeguard           1     biomass_safeguard                   2026
#>  8 multiplier                  0.5   precautionary_multiplier            2026
#>  9 initial_catch_advice     1450.    advice                              2026
#> 10 stability_clause_applied    0     advice                              2026
#> 11 catch_advice             1450.    advice                              2026
#> 12 advice_change              10     advice                              2026

multiplier_lookup() prints a reminder that K ≥ 0.32 means the chr rule; fproxy_rule() stops for K < 0.32 (use the rfb rule) and for K ≥ 0.45.

Pitfalls

  • Units: the harvest rate is landings / index, so both must be in the same units (tonnes). The proxy is only meaningful for the same index as the advice uses.
  • Whose landings: 04-whg uses all countries’ landings in 5.a, as in the harvest rate of its history table. The old chr_rule.R used Icelandic landings only. Choose deliberately: it changes the proxy.
  • Reference years: the old 04-whg code wrote 1985:tyr-1, which in R is 1984:(tyr - 1). 1984 has no index, so the result was the same; write 1985:(assessment_year - 1).
  • The index past the assessment year: the advice uses the last index value, so a later year changes it completely. chr_advice() cuts the index; fproxy_rule() does not.
  • Itrigger: if Itrigger is NULL, fproxy_rule() uses 1.4 × the lowest index value it is given and says so only with cat(). Pass it from ref_points_iloss().
